requirement: The `habeas` skill's reference on distributed requirements MUST give the guidance of {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.when`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.queries`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.site_text`, and {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.reviews` as a list of things to do and a list of things not to do.
rationale:
The `habeas` skill's reference, `assets/skills/habeas/references/distributed-requirements.md`, has a `## Do` list and a `## Don't` list. Each part's guidance appears as an item in one of them.

**`distributed_guidance.when`**
- Make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each site, and use `{impl}` when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole. This is the first Do item.
- Mark `{impl}` on the code that carries out obligations the sites do not uphold. This is the Do item "Separate obligations each site upholds from obligations particular code carries out, and mark that code `{impl}`."

**`distributed_guidance.queries`**
- Site queries must select every place and no others. This is the Do item "check that the site queries select every place the obligation applies and no others", with advice to widen or narrow the query.
- Violation queries for every kind of construct that could break the obligation. This is the Do item "Write a violation query, with `within` naming the site query, for every kind of construct…".
- `match` and `no_match` snippets for every query. This is the Do item "Give every query `match` and `no_match` snippets…", which also says it applies to violation queries.

**`distributed_guidance.site_text`**
- Describe sites exactly as the queries select them, and state any convention the queries rely on as an obligation. Both are in one Do item.
- State only per-site obligations a reviewer can check. This is the Don't item "Don't state a per-site obligation that a reviewer cannot check from the site and the helpers it calls".
- The Don't item "Don't describe sites more broadly than the queries select" reinforces the first of these.

**`distributed_guidance.reviews`**
- Sites need no reference to the requirement. This is the Don't item "Don't reference the distributed requirement from a site just because it is a site; sites need none".
- `habeas author --all` authors the site reviews. This is the Do item "Let `habeas author --all` author the site reviews."
- A false site review is fixed by fixing the site or tightening the queries or text, not by re-running it. This is the Don't item "Don't re-run a false site review for a different result…", and it points to the `habeas-evidence` reference on reviews. The `lists` requirement only asks that this guidance appear in the lists, and it does.

**Test**
`tests/authoring_cli.rs#fn[bundled_skills_give_distributed_guidance_as_do_and_dont_lists]` carries `{test}` for `lists`. It does three things:
- It splits out the `## Do` and `## Don't` sections.
- It checks that each has at least two list items and that Don't items all start with "- Don't ".
- It asserts, through `section` and `assert_text`, that the guidance phrases for all four parts occur in those two lists. `section` collapses whitespace, so the wrapped lines in the file still match.

I found no unspecified behavior and no untested obligation.

text: The `habeas` skill's reference on distributed requirements MUST give the guidance of {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.when`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.queries`, {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.site_text`, and {cite}`requirements.cli.distributed_guidance.reviews` as a list of things to do and a list of things not to do.

The bundled skills MUST direct agents to make a requirement distributed only when its obligation applies on its own at each of many sites, such as a convention every validation function follows; to use `{impl}` instead when particular code carries out the requirement as a whole; and to mark with `{impl}` the code that carries out any obligation of a distributed requirement that its sites do not uphold.

The bundled skills MUST direct agents to write site queries that select every place the obligation applies and no others, violation queries for every kind of construct that could break it, and, for every query, `match` and `no_match` snippets that test its conditions.

The bundled skills MUST direct agents to describe sites exactly as the site queries select them, to state as an obligation any convention the queries rely on, such as how a list is named, and to state only per-site obligations that a reviewer can check from the site and the helpers it calls.

The bundled skills MUST tell agents that sites need no reference to the requirement, that `habeas author --all` authors site reviews under {cite}`requirements.references.site_review`, and that a false site review is addressed by fixing the site, or by tightening the queries or the requirement text when the site should not be covered or the text admits more than one reading, under {cite}`requirements.cli.flip_guidance`, not by re-running the review.
